## Reproduced projection/validation regression in PR #92

Tested commit: [0d30ec217955a12155038726a757bc8c441c2713](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/pull/92). This finding concerns the proposed admission path, not a claim that the released package already refuses this input.

The new [JSON Unicode validation](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/0d30ec217955a12155038726a757bc8c441c2713/admission-schema.ts#L34-L36) rejects unpaired surrogates. The existing [item-state projection](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/0d30ec217955a12155038726a757bc8c441c2713/index.ts#L566-L588) uses UTF-16 `slice(0, 4000)` for text fields and `slice(0, 128)` for tags. These can split an emoji and create malformed Unicode from a valid tracker item. The new mandatory admission path then refuses its own projection as `invalid_input`.

### Expected and actual

The documented projection goal is bounded, least-privilege item state. Valid source text should remain valid after truncation while preserving size/token limits and strict rejection of genuinely malformed source input.

For `"a".repeat(3999) + "😀" + "z"`, the original title is well-formed. Projection retains the first half of the emoji at code-unit index 3999, followed by the truncation suffix. Admission rejects it before inference.

### Sanitized reproduction

An isolated Node source-excerpt harness ran the actual `projectItemState`/`truncateStateText` composition and the new JSON validation helper:

```js
const original = "a".repeat(3999) + "😀" + "z";
original.isWellFormed();                  // true
validate({ title: original });            // accepted
const projected = projectItemState({
  title: original, type: "Task", status: "open", tags: []
});
projected.title.isWellFormed();           // false
projected.title.charCodeAt(3999).toString(16); // "d83d"
validate(projected);                      // throws invalid_input
```

The same code-unit boundary issue applies to tag projection at 128, though the executed reproduction above covers the text-field boundary.

### Impact and limits

A valid long title/body/description can block decision commands merely because an emoji crosses the projection limit. This is a reproduced source-composition defect, not evidence of a provider-side tokenizer failure. No SDK installation, provider request, inference, full CLI run or mutation was performed.

### Regression criteria

- Test a supplementary Unicode character spanning the 4,000-code-unit text boundary and the 128-code-unit tag boundary.
- Generated projections remain well-formed and pass admission when the original source is valid.
- Maintain bounded projection size and token admission; do not remove the Unicode validator or silently allow malformed input.
- Retain short-Unicode and ordinary ASCII truncation controls, and rejection coverage for actual unpaired surrogates.

### Scope and deduplication

The source goal is tracked by [pm-jev-tokenizer-admission](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-jev/blob/0d30ec217955a12155038726a757bc8c441c2713/.agents/pm/features/pm-jev-tokenizer-admission.toon). Before filing, the review screened all 92 all-status issue/PR titles, all four ordinary issue bodies, all 49 canonical PM records at this commit, the fresh #92 discussion and related #47 discussion. No existing issue or canonical defect record covered this mechanism. Historical PR conversations were not exhaustively audited. The candidate head was rechecked unchanged immediately before filing.
PR #92 rejects valid Unicode after item-state truncation splits a surrogate pair
